title: Faster robot computing, built in Pune.
standfirst: Prateek Nagras started TechnoYantra in Pune, then partnered with Acceleration Robotics in Spain and became its CEO. His Indian team, Technoyantra Robotics Private Limited, works under the Acceleration Robotics brand to make ROS 2 workloads run faster and more efficiently, and has helped bring India’s ROS community together with ARTPARK.

hero.alt: Four engineers looking at a laptop beside parts of a robotic arm on a workbench
hero.caption: Engineers with a robotic arm in an ARTPARK lab. ARTPARK photograph, not of Acceleration Robotics.

lead: “When I started TechnoYantra in 2019, the ROS robotics industry in Asia was just getting started, but since the pandemic as people have become more and more accepting of working together with robots, the robot deployments have grown exponentially,” says Prateek Nagras, CEO of Acceleration Robotics.

Prateek started TechnoYantra in Pune. It later partnered with Acceleration Robotics in Spain, and following that partnership he became CEO of Acceleration Robotics. In India the company is Technoyantra Robotics Private Limited, operating under the Acceleration Robotics brand from Aundh, Pune. Its work is robotics computing: making ROS 2 workloads faster and more efficient.

blocks: Most robots today run on the Robot Operating System, or ROS. As robots take on harder perception and motion-planning work, they need more computing power and lower latency. The chips that could provide it, FPGAs, GPUs and CPUs, come from an industry that thinks about its own roadmaps, not about robots.

Prateek described the problem to Electronics For You in 2023: “there is a big gap between the semiconductor industry, which is basically manufacturing the FPGAs and GPUs and CPUs, and the robotics industry, where they consume these chips to unveil their own software stacks on top of it.”

The team’s answer is the ROBOTCORE product family, hardware acceleration on GPUs and FPGAs, benchmarking of robotic workloads, and the engineering and integration support needed to bring all of this into real robot systems.

panel.title: What the team works on
items: A hardware acceleration framework for ROS and ROS 2 that works across GPU and FPGA vendors.
A robot processing unit for ROS, which the company lists with 16 CPUs, a GPU and an FPGA.
Accelerated ROS 2, RTPS and UDP/IP. The company says it sends and receives small packets in 700 nanoseconds.
Measuring the performance of robotic workloads, including with ROBOTPERF.
Robot IP core design and engineering services to bring acceleration into robot systems, with case studies listed for CELSA and Teknia.

blocks: In 2023, Prateek described what might come next: “Right now we are just concentrating on software and use off-the shelf hardware, but maybe in a few years, we could even start building our own custom hardware dedicated for robots, so we can basically have our own hardware plus software combination.”

TechnoYantra was a Pune consultancy specialising in ROS. In November 2022 it partnered with Acceleration Robotics, a robotics semiconductor company headquartered in Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain. Following the partnership, Prateek became CEO, his colleague Gaurav Vikhe became Chief Product Officer, and Acceleration Robotics’ founder, Víctor Mayoral-Vilches, became CTO. The group said it had served more than 20 clients between them, including Xilinx and AMD.

Víctor, a roboticist who had earlier co-founded Erle Robotics and founded Alias Robotics, had launched ROBOTCORE in June 2022 and announced a collaboration with AMD that September to design robotic compute architectures with ROS.

quote.text: Given the struggles of the semiconductor industry to efficiently cater to this demand, this seemed to me to be the perfect time to start a new journey with Acceleration Robotics and bridge the gap between semiconductor manufacturers and ROS.

people.name: Víctor Mayoral-Vilches
people.role: Founder of Acceleration Robotics, Spain · CTO from November 2022

sections.h2: Building a ROS community in India.
blocks: By April 2024, Emprendedores reported, the company had more than 15 people working remotely, half of them in India, including the CEO. It had taken no external funding.

In India the team has also helped gather the people who use ROS, working with ARTPARK. In March 2023, Acceleration Robotics held a ROS developers meet-up at IISc, Bengaluru, in collaboration with ARTPARK, opened by Prof. Bharadwaj Amrutur. In December 2023, ROSCon India was co-hosted by Acceleration Robotics and RigBetel Labs and powered by ARTPARK at IISc. The second edition followed in December 2024 at IISc, Bengaluru, hosted by the same two companies, powered by ARTPARK-IISc and held in association with Open Robotics. In December 2025 the third ROSCon India moved to COEP Technological University in Pune, again hosted by RigBetel Labs and Acceleration Robotics and powered by ARTPARK and IISc, with Open Robotics. Acceleration Robotics is part of ARTPARK’s startup portfolio.
